description: Delacroix paints the Three Glorieuses: Marianne with the flag, mixed people, barricades. Political romanticism enters the museum.

hero.hook: A woman with the flag, and the Revolution becomes an image again.

blocks.text: Posters, tickets, school memoirs: the image has gone beyond the table. It establishes the idea of ​​a freedom that is won in smoke.
To fully understand Liberty Leading the People, Delacroix, you must keep one thing in mind: each technical detail serves an emotion or an idea. The work is never just decorative.
Context matters as much as style. Dates, places, sponsors, public: all this explains why a form appears at a specific moment, and not before.
Finally, legacy is measured over the long term. What we see today in museums, films or popular music still bears the traces of these inventions.
From the street of 1830 to school textbooks, the work has established an imagination: freedom is won, it is not just contemplated.
